title: Report a scam text
body: All major UK networks let you report suspicious texts free by forwarding them to 7726. Your provider can investigate and block the sender.

title: Report a suspicious email
body: The National Cyber Security Centre investigates reported emails and has removed hundreds of thousands of scam web pages. Screenshots are accepted too.

title: Speak to your bank safely
body: 159 connects you to your own bank's fraud team. It works for over 99% of UK current accounts and cannot be spoofed. Never use a number from the message itself.

title: Report fraud to the police
body: If you lost money or shared personal details, report it to Report Fraud (England, Wales and Northern Ireland) online or on 0300 123 2040.

title: Report fraud in Scotland
body: In Scotland, fraud is reported to Police Scotland by calling 101.

title: Report an HMRC scam text
body: HMRC scam texts can be forwarded to 60599. Network charges apply — 7726 remains the free general route.

title: Report an HMRC scam email or WhatsApp
body: HMRC investigates emails, WhatsApp messages and QR-code emails claiming to be from HMRC. HMRC never texts or emails about rebates or refunds.

title: Check an investment offer
body: Before investing, check the firm on the FCA register and warning list. Unregistered firms have no UK protection, and 'guaranteed returns' do not exist.

title: If you transferred money
body: Banks must generally reimburse authorised push payment fraud on Faster Payments and CHAPS up to £85,000, usually within 5 business days. Contact your bank first, then Report Fraud.
